source.title: Convex Dual Theory Analysis of Two-Layer Convolutional Neural Networks With Soft-Thresholding
source.authors: Chunyan Xiong; Chao-Xing Zhang; Meng Lu; Xiaotong Yu; Jian Cao; Zhong Chen; D. Guo; X. Qu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares training outcomes under different optimizers and initializations in a two-layer soft-thresholding CNN, using denoising objective values rather than the classification-error measures in the claim.
record.gate_note: Experiments use MNIST image denoising with a 600-image training set, not CIFAR classification. Reported optimizer and initialization comparisons bear on V4's initialization component, but the paper does not test signal or gradient propagation, learning speed, or trainable depth. Its dual-network comparisons are part of the study's proposed convexification method.
record.test_reason: The study measures optimizer- and initialization-dependent denoising objective values in a two-layer soft-thresholding CNN. It does not measure V4's learning speed, trainable depth, or signal and gradient preservation, and its results do not test any other supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors claim a strong-duality proof for sufficiently many convolution filters and propose the convex dual to remove initialization dependence. Their denoising experiments show close primal and dual objectives with ADAM and Kaiming uniform initialization; they acknowledge small numerical gaps. They also report optimizer and initialization dependence of the primal network.
record.recipe_differences: Two-layer soft-thresholding convolutional network trained for MNIST denoising; compares primal and proposed convex dual formulations, rather than benchmark classification training.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the primal ST-CNN's optimal solution depends on optimizer choice and that its objective comparison with the dual network changes with initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that primal ST-CNN objective outcomes depend on optimizer selection, without readable optimizer-specific values in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects achieved objectives in the tested two-layer soft-thresholding CNN denoising task.

fits_no_version.finding: Primal and dual objectives coincide under Kaiming uniform initialization; the dual achieves a better objective under normal initializations with standard deviations 0.001 and 0.005.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization affects the achieved denoising objective of the tested primal soft-thresholding CNN relative to its proposed convex dual.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: The experiments use MNIST denoising rather than classification benchmarks. Fig. 8 and Fig. 9 are described without numeric objective values in the text. The paper gives no uncertainty estimates or capability check.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Fig. 8 optimizer-specific values are figure-only and cannot be assigned numeric outcomes from the text; they are retained as separate rows.

untested.parts: CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and model-size or training-recipe effects.
ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and deep plain or normalization-free residual training.
Initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth; signal and gradient preservation; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization; very deep convolutional training.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, loss transients, curvature evolution, and divergence.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V4 limits_scope verdict: achieved objective quality is a different outcome from the speed and depth effects V4 specifies. The supplied figures contain captions but no readable curves or numerical values.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR training classification error, corrupted or random labels, model size, and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network depth comparisons, shortcuts, ImageNet or CIFAR training, and the cited special methods.
Signal and gradient propagation, learning speed, trainable depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Training above a stability limit, curvature or sharpness changes, and divergence thresholds.
Batch normalization comparisons, accuracy gain, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

reader_labels.condition: Kaiming He uniform initialization versus normal initializations with standard deviations 0.001 and 0.005
reader_labels.reason: Objective values coincide with Kaiming He uniform initialization, while the dual objective is better than the primal objective under both stated normal initializations; see R4–R6. This is a denoising objective comparison, not a learning-speed or depth result.
